A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local routing consistency study, with matching methods and model identities. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite expanded evaluation coverage and rearranged material.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing analyses across 20 MoE models, including SRP/SCH measurements, specialization analyses, post-training comparisons, and bootstrap confidence intervals.

after.justification: v2 reports original analyses on the expanded corpus, retains the supplementary model analyses, and adds correlations between SCH and practical cache-policy hit rates.

M1.justification: The activation collection, threshold search maximizing SRP, and frequency-ranked oracle calculation of SCH remain unchanged in Sections 2–3. The added datasets and cache-policy comparisons do not introduce a new proposed routing or offloading procedure.

E1.justification: v1 uses seven RedPajama domains. v2 adds LMArena preferred conversations, OpenMathInstruct-2, OpenCodeInstruct, and OpenScienceReasoning-2, substantially extending coverage to conversational and instruction/reasoning text. These datasets support routing analysis, not downstream task-accuracy evaluation.

E2.justification: v2 Section 5.2 and Table 3 add LRU, LFU, and fixed caching as evaluated comparators for SCH through hit-rate correlations. v1 discusses caching policies but does not report this comparison. The 20-model roster and base/post-trained comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The corpus grows from 14,336 to 22,528 sequences. v2 introduces preferred-conversation filtering and role/content concatenation for LMArena, plus input/output concatenation for the instruction datasets. It also adds cache-policy correlation evaluation across four segment lengths. The 512-token length, 2,048 sequences per domain, model configurations, and encoder-decoder preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused practical-validity analysis asking whether oracle SCH correlates with cache-policy hit rates. Domain-specialization and cross-domain correlation analyses incorporate the added domains. Existing position, layer, perplexity, and post-training analyses remain; the SRP–SCH correlation analysis moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix E.6.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% SCH confidence intervals using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. v1 Appendix D.1/Table 5 becomes v2 Appendix E.7/Table 8. Changed interval endpoints are result updates; v2 introduces no specified repeated-run counts, seeds, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The expanded corpus produces revised aggregate scores, rankings, specialization results, and confidence intervals. Table 1 changes LLaMA-MoE-v2 SRP from 79.59 to 78.16 and Qwen3 from 55.90 to 54.14, with PowerMoE overtaking Qwen3. These are different-corpus results, not same-setting performance changes. New Table 3 reports SCH correlations at m = 16 of 90.43 for LRU, 88.70 for LFU, and 89.79 for fixed caching.

T1.justification: The SRP, routing-size ratio, and SCH definitions and Equations 1–15 retain their mathematical substance. The proofs move from Appendix B to Appendix C; a stray multiplication dot is removed without changing the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the two metrics, the architecture and specialization findings, and the approximately 2x cache-size recommendation. The added experiments provide support for these existing claims without introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a conjecture that dense modules weaken routing signals and specialization, distinguishes math/coding specialization from generic-text specialization, and interprets cache-policy correlations as evidence of practical relevance. An introductory footnote frames the 2x recommendation as model-design guidance. The explicit limitations paragraph concerning sub-60B coverage and real-system validation is removed, although Section 5.2 still acknowledges SCH's oracle nature.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds concrete preprocessing instructions for the new datasets. A new reproducibility statement reports deterministic corpus construction and experimental configuration and promises release of the sampled corpus and source code. The existing abstract code link and hardware/BF16 disclosures remain; the PDFs do not establish that the promised additional resources are available.

R1.justification: v2 adds the four dataset references and cites Guo et al. (2025) and Chen et al. (2025) on reinforcing expert specialization. Appendix B.2 more explicitly distinguishes this study from earlier short-span and input-level locality observations. The overall research positioning remains intact; the Qwen3 citation changes from its announcement to its technical report.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, condenses the main-text model inventory, reorganizes supplementary analyses, and moves the SRP–SCH discussion into the appendix. It adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements and changes numerical citations to author–year style. The main six-section narrative and most definitions and proofs remain structurally similar.

P2.justification: v2 adds the cache-policy Table 3 and transposes and relocates the former Table 3 as Table 7. Figure 3 and heatmaps 8–9 expand to eleven domains; Figure 5 gains group-specific line styles, and several expert plots adjust axis ranges. Retained displays are reordered or relocated within the same general visual design.

improvement.justification: The broader application-oriented corpus and new cache-policy correlations improve empirical relevance and provide some validation beyond comparisons between oracle metrics. The gain is limited by sparse reporting of the cache-policy settings and the absence of end-to-end offloading measurements. Removing the explicit limitations paragraph also weakens qualification, but the additional empirical evidence supports a modest net improvement.
